newsitem.title: UK: Pension head's suspension adds to DMG woes.
newsitem.headline: Pension head's suspension adds to DMG woes.

text.p: Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, the investment banking arm of Germany's Deutsche Bank, on Tuesday suspended another of its London-based employees.

DMG said the suspension of 35-year-old Nicola Horlick, head of Morgan Grenfell Asset Management's British pension fund business, was not related to investigations into last year's scandal at three of its investment trusts.

"We have suspended her today pending the outcome of an internal investigation which will look at a potential breach of her contract. It has nothing to do with the Peter Young affair nor any suggestion of financial impropriety," DMG spokesman James Murray told Reuters.

Last year, MGAM fund manager Young was sacked for gross misconduct after irregularities were discovered in valuations and the funds were temporarily suspended. MGAM's parent Deutsche stepped in with a 180 million pound ($301.1 million) cash injection to buy out the suspect securities and ensure trading in the funds resumed.
Young, who has denied involvement in any criminal activity, is being investigated by Britain's Serious Fraud Office.

The affair has already led to high-level casualties at MGAM. In October a number of senior management, including chief executive Keith Percy and three other directors, left the firm. DMG said the departures were due to "management failings".

And in December the cost to Deutsche Bank rose when it agreed to a record compensation package of around 200 million pounds ($334.5 million) to make good losses to investors who lost out as a result of the affair.
MGAM is still under investigation by investments watchdog the Investment Management Regulatory Organisation (IMRO), which is expected to make its findings during the first quarter of the year.

An IMRO spokeswoman told Reuters Horlick's suspension was "not connected to Peter Young affair and is not a regulatory matter", adding it was not appropriate to comment "on matters relating to its firms and what they may be doing with regards to their staff".
Earlier the Evening Standard newspaper said Horlick was "understood to have been on the brink of leaving her job and attempting to take a number of colleagues with her".
Dutch bank ABN AMRO declined to comment on reports that Horlick was on the verge of joining the firm. However banking sources dismissed the idea that Horlick was set to join the Dutch bank.
Although one banking source added,"She's an extremely successful fund manager and I'm sure she's on a lot of people's shopping lists."

Murray said DMG would complete its probe into the potential breach of contract by Horlick "as quickly as possible" but said her suspension was "purely internal" and had no regulatory dimension or link to last year's events.

Horlick, whose husband Timothy is chief operating officer of European investment banking at U.S. investment bank Salomon Brothers in London, has five children. Before joining Morgan Grenfell five years ago she worked at Mercury Asset Management, where Peter Young worked as a fund manager before joining MGAM. ($1=.5979 Pound)
